subject: POC capacity planning - Acme AI - reserved GPUs & autoscale
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC capacity planning — next steps

Thanks for the call today, Marissa — good alignment across both sides. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can lock the POC timeline: 

- Primary evaluation workload: multi-turn retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) at ~1.2k tokens per session, peak concurrent sessions expected ~120 during demo windows.
- Success criteria: 99th percentile latency < 600ms for generation at 1.2k tokens, end-to-end throughput to support 120 concurrent sessions for 15-minute demo windows, and no more than 2% token generation error rate across 3 test prompts.
- Timeline: target POC start 2027-05-09, 2-week run, final review week of 2027-05-23.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood reserve baseline capacity for the POC (we were thinking 2 x A100 equivalent GPUs) and allow burst up to 8 GPUs during demo windows?
2) What autoscaling behavior would you recommend to keep costs predictable while meeting the latency SLO?
3) Can you send a short doc with the proposed capacity plan and expected costs for our review?

Appreciate a short proposal we can share with our infra and procurement.

Best,
Samir
Head of ML Ops, Acme AI
samir@acme.ai
(415) 555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 19:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning — next steps

Thanks Samir — great to meet. Appreciate the clear success criteria and timeline. See proposed plan below; attaching a one-page capacity plan and POC runbook for your infra/procurement (acme-poc-capacity-plan-v2.pdf, acme-poc-mop.xlsx).

Proposed POC capacity & ops (summary):
- Baseline reserved capacity: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) for baseline throughput.
- Burst capacity: allow on-demand burst up to 8 GPUs via Dedicated burst pool during scheduled demo windows (we recommend booking burst in advance for guaranteed availability).
- Autoscaling policy: scale based on token/second and queue latency thresholds; target scale-up when 95th pct queue latency > 200ms, scale down after 3m of sustained low load. We’ll enforce a max ramp of +2 GPUs per minute to avoid sudden cost spikes.
- KV/prefix caching: enable Redis-backed prefix caching for prompt prefixes (expected to reduce per-token compute by ~15% for your RAG pattern).
- Cost estimate (rough): baseline reserved (2 GPUs) ~ $X/day, anticipated burst usage (up to 8 GPUs for 2 hours across demo days) additional ~ $Y. Final numbers in attached spreadsheet.

Success criteria mapping (how Redwood will measure):
- 99th pct generation latency measured at application-level (< 600ms) — telemetry hooks and per-token breakdown in the Console.
- Throughput verification: load test simulating 120 concurrent sessions with target token distribution.
- Error rate: we’ll monitor generation errors and model fallback ratio; threshold for pass is < 2%.

Next steps / owners: 
- Marissa (Redwood) to provide capacity plan and POC runbook: attached (today).
- Lukas (Redwood SE) to schedule an infra sync and run initial load test (propose 2027-05-04).
- Samir / Priya (Acme) to confirm POC start date and procurement approval for reserved capacity (target 2027-05-09).

If that looks good I’ll loop in our infra team to provision reserved GPUs and set the autoscale policy.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-poc-capacity-plan-v2.pdf, acme-poc-mop.xlsx

From: Priya Shah <priya@acme.ai>

Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.ai>, sales@acme.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning — next steps

Thanks Marissa — the plan looks good overall. A few follow-ups from procurement / infra before we lock dates: 

- Procurement wants firm SKU and reservation window for the baseline (i.e., which GPU type and whether a monthly reservation applies). For the POC we can approve a 2-week reservation if we get a clear daily cost estimate.
- Infra asks if Redwood can guarantee availability for burst up to 8 GPUs during our demo windows (we may book two 1-hour demos on 2027-05-15). If guaranteed burst is not possible, we need a fallback plan that keeps latency within SLOs even without full burst.
- Can you confirm the autoscale cooldown and max ramp (we prefer conservative max ramp to avoid double-scaling across our systems).

If you can send a short note with the confirmed SKU (A100-40GB or equivalent), reservation window (2027-05-09 to 2027-05-22), and an estimated cost for baseline + a 2-hour burst per demo day, procurement can greenlight.

Thanks — Priya
